title: Timeline with Multiple Events

illustrates.quote: Timelines with Multiple Events in the Same Year. Use a nested list format when a date has more than one event. Place the date at the left margin (cell 1). Use 3-5 margins for each following event. (See Sample 6-10: Timeline with Multiple Events on page 6-28.)

figure.description: A timeline from 1050 to 1650 with events at various points; two events share the date 1438.

print.notes: Per 6.10.3: the shared date 1438 sits alone at cell 1 (its own list item), with its two events nested at 3-5 margins below it (6.10.3's own worked example). '1050'/'1200'/'1350'/'1500'/'1650' are the timeline's own axis ticks (6.10.1c/d: only the first and last dates, plus every date with an associated event, are kept) — this excerpt only transcribes '1050' and '1650' of those (the middle ticks, and the 1200/1350/1500 axis marks with no event, are omitted by the book's own excerpt, not built).
print.printFeatures: Timeline diagram: a horizontal line with dated callout boxes.

braille.notes: Date 1438 (cell 1) is followed by its two same-year events at 3-5 margins (cell 3), per 6.10.3.

uncertain: 'c. 1100 Incas settle in Cuzco.': the agreed braille has no letter-indicator (';') before the abbreviation 'c.', but Emboss's own translator (the same liblouis en-ueb-g2 table gold-run.mjs itself uses) adds one when forward-translating a standalone 'c.' in isolation or with surrounding context tried here — confirmed by direct experiment, not assumed. This looks like a genuine liblouis UEB Grade-2 rule difference (single-letter abbreviation before a period not needing the letter sign) rather than a transcription error in either run, and is expected to produce a narrow, one-cell mismatch on this line specifically when gold-run.mjs is executed.
resolution: B's braille margins (2-space runover for the two nested 1438 events, 12-space heading indent) match the raw source exactly (source-6.txt lines 5060-5069, decoded directly); A's runover is 1 space short and its heading indent 1 short. All dates/text confirmed by exact forward-translation except the 'c.' abbreviation noted above. print.blocks[2] (the actual buildable list, with the 1438/nested-events structure) was built here since neither run supplied one, only a flat, unordered figure.labels array.
